transcription: I replied to a stranger's email by mistake. Three years later, I was giving a toast at his wedding. About three years ago, I got an email meant for someone else. It was a classic Gmail mishap one letter off. The message was short and kind of urgent hey man, are we still good for dinner on Friday? Liz's cooking and she made that lasagna you love. I had no clue who Liz was, but I was having a rough week in the thought of home cooked lasagna just. Hit different. So, being half bored and fully nosy, I replied I think you've got the wrong guy. But now I'm emotionally invested in this lasagna plan. Please tell Liz I believe in her. Didn't expect a reply. But I got one. Wrong guy but best reply I've gotten in months. I'll keep you posted on the lasagna. That's how it started. Me, and a guy named Eric from Ohio. We ended up exchanging emails for weeks. Then months. At first, it was dumb jokes, weird food picks, and debates about which animal would win in a fight spoiler he was firmly team octopus. But then came the deeper stuff job stress, break up rants, grieving a friend. And suddenly this stranger from a lasagna email became someone I trusted more than half the people in my actual life. After about a year, we finally met IRL when I had a work trip near him. We had tacos and beers and talk like old college roommates. Fast forward to last summer Eric invites me to his wedding. I think he was half joking. I said yes before he could change his mind. It was small, beautiful, and full of people who had clearly known him forever. Then, out of nowhere, his new wife stands up and says, before the speeches, I want to thank the person who helped Eric.
